title: Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS — Premium Revision Paper #16

pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The kayamba is a shaker used mainly at the (1 mark)
   A. Northern desert only
   B. Kenyan coast
   C. North of Lake Victoria only
   D. Kenyan highlands only

2. Who must do the burning when making charcoal sticks? (1 mark)
   A. Any learner
   B. An adult or the teacher
   C. The youngest learner
   D. Nobody

3. Percussion instruments make sound when they are (1 mark)
   A. bowed with a stick of hair
   B. blown with air only
   C. struck, shaken or scraped
   D. sung into

4. A melodic percussion instrument is one that (1 mark)
   A. can only make one sound
   B. is always loud
   C. can play different notes to make a tune
   D. has no parts

5. To make a very dark tone with charcoal you should (1 mark)
   A. press very lightly
   B. use water
   C. use no charcoal
   D. press harder

6. What is the main reason for improvising a netball? (1 mark)
   A. To avoid playing
   B. Because real balls are always bad
   C. To spend more money
   D. To use available materials when balls are not enough

7. Which is a good safety rule before playing netball? (1 mark)
   A. Play on broken ground
   B. Wear a necklace
   C. Remove rings and bracelets
   D. Play with long sharp nails

8. How long may a player hold the ball before passing or shooting? (1 mark)
   A. One minute
   B. Ten seconds
   C. As long as they like
   D. Three seconds

9. Which players are allowed to shoot at goal? (1 mark)
   A. GK and GD
   B. GS and GA
   C. Only C
   D. WA and WD

10. How many secondary colours are there on the basic colour wheel? (1 mark)
   A. Nine
   B. Six
   C. Three
   D. Two

11. After painting, how should you store a brush? (1 mark)
   A. Under a heavy book
   B. Standing on its hairs in water
   C. Washed and laid flat or with hairs upwards
   D. Covered in paint

12. What does a crotchet look like? (1 mark)
   A. A zigzag
   B. A dot only
   C. A filled-in oval with a stem
   D. An empty circle

13. How many guide lines are used for practising lettering in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Six
   B. Two
   C. Four
   D. Ten

14. The French rhythm name for a pair of quavers is (1 mark)
   A. taa
   B. ta-te
   C. rest
   D. tee-taa

15. Which melody uses only steps? (1 mark)
   A. d d m d
   B. d m d m
   C. d r m r d
   D. m d m d

16. At the set position, the hips are (1 mark)
   A. a little higher than the shoulders
   B. lower than the knees
   C. behind the line only
   D. on the ground

17. Which part of the foot should touch the ground when sprinting? (1 mark)
   A. The heel
   B. The ankle
   C. The front part of the foot
   D. The side only

18. A relay race is a race in which (1 mark)
   A. one person runs all the way
   B. people throw a ball
   C. people jump into sand
   D. team members take turns running and pass a baton

19. How should we treat the national flag? (1 mark)
   A. Write on it
   B. Throw it around
   C. Use it as a rag
   D. With care and respect, never letting it touch the ground

20. On the Kenyan flag, black stands for (1 mark)
   A. the sea
   B. the people of Kenya
   C. the land
   D. peace

21. Why do we warm up before sprinting? (1 mark)
   A. To make the track smooth
   B. To tire out the muscles
   C. To hide from the starter
   D. To prepare muscles and avoid injury

22. Which should you remove before gymnastics? (1 mark)
   A. Your clothes
   B. Your smile
   C. Watches and bracelets
   D. Your hair

23. Why is gymnastics described as not being a race? (1 mark)
   A. It uses no body
   B. It cannot be seen
   C. It is about control and quality, not speed
   D. It is always in the dark

24. Which quality do rolls and balances build? (1 mark)
   A. Reading speed
   B. Loud singing
   C. Colour mixing
   D. Balance and coordination

25. Dynamics means (1 mark)
   A. the words
   B. how loud or soft the music is
   C. the speed
   D. the pitch

26. Which facial expression fits a joyful song? (1 mark)
   A. Closed eyes
   B. A yawn
   C. A smile
   D. A frown

27. When you give feedback on a friend's photograph you should (1 mark)
   A. say it is terrible
   B. say nothing
   C. laugh
   D. say what you like first and then suggest one improvement

28. After taking photos, choosing the best ones is called (1 mark)
   A. hiding
   B. selecting
   C. painting
   D. smudging

29. Which photo should be kept? (1 mark)
   A. One that is dark and blurred
   B. One taken by accident
   C. One with good light and a clear centre of interest
   D. One with a finger on the lens

30. Another name for the descant recorder is the (1 mark)
   A. drum
   B. soprano recorder
   C. xylophone
   D. bass recorder

31. Where should the mouthpiece rest? (1 mark)
   A. On your chin
   B. Between your teeth
   C. Behind your ear
   D. Between your lips, not your teeth

32. On the staff, the note A sits (1 mark)
   A. on line 1
   B. above the staff
   C. below the staff
   D. in the space between lines 2 and 3

33. A swimming cap is useful for (1 mark)
   A. keeping long hair out of the way
   B. making you float
   C. drying
   D. holding a whistle

34. Who can teach you an indigenous game from your community? (1 mark)
   A. An elder
   B. A stranger online
   C. Only a computer
   D. Nobody

35. Animal games improve (1 mark)
   A. only singing
   B. fitness and health
   C. only reading
   D. only cooking

36. Indigenous games are (1 mark)
   A. games from space
   B. games played only with computers
   C. games with no rules
   D. traditional games that belong to a people and place

37. Which material can you use to make a portfolio? (1 mark)
   A. Manila paper or cardboard
   B. Iron sheets
   C. Sand
   D. Glass

38. When presenting your artwork, you should hold it (1 mark)
   A. upside down
   B. by the middle with wet hands
   C. by one corner and shake
   D. carefully by the edges

39. The Kenya National Anthem is called (1 mark)
   A. Twinkle Twinkle Little Star
   B. Ee Mungu Nguvu Yetu
   C. Malaika
   D. Jambo Bwana

40. Works on display should be kept away from (1 mark)
   A. water, direct sun and dust
   B. shelves
   C. other pictures
   D. walls

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give three ways of caring for a digital camera. (3 marks)

42. Why does a recorder squeak when you blow too hard? (2 marks)

43. What is the difference between tempo and dynamics? (2 marks)

44. State four things to think about when analysing an art work. (4 marks)

45. Describe how to get into a crab balance. (4 marks)

46. State what the colours black and green stand for on the Kenyan flag. (2 marks)

47. Why do singers use hand signs? (2 marks)

48. Why is light important in photography? (2 marks)

49. Explain the steps of a full sprint from the start commands to the finish. (5 marks)

50. Give four ways of caring for displayed works. (4 marks)

51. Why do we improvise a netball? (3 marks)

52. Describe how to make a portfolio from manila paper. (5 marks)

53. Explain how you decide whether a percussion instrument is melodic or non-melodic. (3 marks)

54. State what red, white and the shield stand for on the Kenyan flag. (3 marks)

55. Why is gymnastics not a race? (2 marks)

56. Describe how to critique a friend's rhythmic pattern with respect. (4 marks)

57. Describe how to present an artwork from your portfolio. (4 marks)

58. Describe how to learn the East African Community anthem for performance. (4 marks)

59. Why do we use a streamlined shape when gliding? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #16 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Kenyan coast
   The kayamba is a coastal shaker used by the Mijikenda and other coastal people.

2. B — An adult or the teacher
   Fire is dangerous, so only an adult does the burning.

3. C — struck, shaken or scraped
   A percussion instrument is played by hitting, shaking or scraping it.

4. C — can play different notes to make a tune
   Melodic instruments such as the xylophone play notes of different pitch.

5. D — press harder
   Pressing harder leaves more charcoal, so the tone is darker.

6. D — To use available materials when balls are not enough
   Improvising lets us practise with materials we already have.

7. C — Remove rings and bracelets
   Jewellery can hurt you and others.

8. D — Three seconds
   A player must pass or shoot within three seconds.

9. B — GS and GA
   Only the Goal Shooter and the Goal Attack may score.

10. C — Three
   Orange, green and purple are the three secondary colours.

11. C — Washed and laid flat or with hairs upwards
   Washing and shaping the tip keeps the brush in good shape.

12. C — A filled-in oval with a stem
   A crotchet has a filled note head and a stem.

13. C — Four
   Ascender line, top of small letters, baseline and descender line make four.

14. B — ta-te
   Ta-te is two short sounds in one beat.

15. C — d r m r d
   Each move in d r m r d is to a neighbouring note.

16. A — a little higher than the shoulders
   On set the hips lift slightly above the shoulders.

17. C — The front part of the foot
   Sprinters land on the balls of the feet.

18. D — team members take turns running and pass a baton
   In a relay, runners pass a baton to the next teammate.

19. D — With care and respect, never letting it touch the ground
   Respect for the flag means caring for it.

20. B — the people of Kenya
   Black represents the people of Kenya.

21. D — To prepare muscles and avoid injury
   Warm muscles work better and are less likely to be hurt.

22. C — Watches and bracelets
   Jewellery can hurt you or others.

23. C — It is about control and quality, not speed
   Skill and control matter more than speed.

24. D — Balance and coordination
   Gymnastics teaches the body to stay steady and move parts together.

25. B — how loud or soft the music is
   Dynamics are the loud and soft parts.

26. C — A smile
   Facial expressions show the mood.

27. D — say what you like first and then suggest one improvement
   Kind and helpful feedback works best.

28. B — selecting
   Selecting means choosing the best.

29. C — One with good light and a clear centre of interest
   Good photographs are well lit and clear.

30. B — soprano recorder
   The descant is the soprano recorder.

31. D — Between your lips, not your teeth
   Lips form the seal.

32. D — in the space between lines 2 and 3
   A is in the space between G and B.

33. A — keeping long hair out of the way
   Caps keep hair tidy.

34. A — An elder
   Elders know many traditional games.

35. B — fitness and health
   They strengthen muscles and improve stamina.

36. D — traditional games that belong to a people and place
   They are passed on by playing together.

37. A — Manila paper or cardboard
   Manila paper folds easily.

38. D — carefully by the edges
   Careful handling keeps it clean.

39. B — Ee Mungu Nguvu Yetu
   The Kiswahili title is Ee Mungu Nguvu Yetu.

40. A — water, direct sun and dust
   Water, sun and dust can damage works.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hold with two hands; use a strap; clean the lens with a soft dry cloth; keep away from water and dust; charge the battery. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: The air is blown too strongly, so the note jumps to a very high shrill sound. Blow more gently.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Tempo is the speed of the music. Dynamics are how loud or soft the music is.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Aesthetic, skills, message and behaviour. Feedback is also accepted.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sit with knees bent and feet flat. Put hands behind you shoulder-width apart with fingers pointing to the feet. Push through hands and feet to lift the hips so the body is level. Hold for a few counts.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Black stands for the people of Kenya. Green stands for the land and its natural wealth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: To show and remember the height of each note, and to help them sing in tune.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for showing pitch, 1 mark for remembering or singing in tune.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Light lets the camera record the picture. With good light the subject is clear.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: On your marks: go to the line and take the position. Set: lift the hips slightly and stay still. Go: push hard and swing the arms. Run in your lane with high knees and bent arms. Keep running through the finish line and slow down gradually.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for marks, set, go, running technique and finishing.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Do not touch or write on them; keep away from water, sun and dust; keep neat labels; store in the portfolio flat afterwards. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Some schools do not have enough balls. We can use materials we have, such as string and waste cloth. It lets more learners practise.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

52. (5 marks)
   Answer: Fold two large pieces of manila paper to make a folder and trim the edges. Punch holes and add a string tie. Paste coloured paper or fabric on the cover. Write a label with name and class. Put in the works with dates and notes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of the five parts.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen to the sounds. If it plays different notes, high and low, that make a tune, it is melodic. If it gives only a beat or one kind of sound, it is non-melodic.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for listening, 1 mark for melodic meaning, 1 mark for non-melodic meaning.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Red stands for the blood shed for freedom. White stands for peace and honesty. The shield and spears stand for the defence of freedom.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is about control and quality of movement, not about speed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for control, 1 mark for not speed.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Say one good thing first. Talk about the steadiness of the beat, variation and the ending. Give one suggestion to make it better. Listen to others' views politely.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Hold it carefully, say the title, explain the materials and skills, tell the message, say what you like and what you would change, and listen to feedback.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: Listen to it several times, read and discuss the words, clap the rhythm, sing line by line and then sing the whole song together in unison while standing straight and respectful.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: A long, thin shape slips through the water easily, so you glide further.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.
